title: Divine Judgment and the Consequences of Sin
english: You have destroyed my land, and you have killed my people; you shall not remain for an age of time, you evil seed.

Prepare your children to be slaughtered by the sins of your father, so that they may not rise up to inherit the land, but rather fill the land with war. 'I will rise up against them,' says the Lord of Hosts, 'and I will destroy their name, their remnant, and their seed.'
Therefore, He says, the name of the Lord shall endure for a long time.
If one were to consider the matter historically, God destroyed Israel through seventy years.

But if one were to sift the inner and hidden meanings like a sieve, it would be understood by the mind that the finder of sin has completed a long duration of time, having placed the yoke of his own misery upon all those on the earth, so that even their own people might become worshippers, and he might leave those of sin ensnared in nooses.
Yet the only-begotten Word of God shone upon us through a long time; and He has become, burning with glory, a word of His lips that is a word full of wrath.

For Cambyses, incited and instigated by God toward war, led an army of the Chaldeans and seized the Babylonians by force. To them, wrath and fire became such a thing; for just as he had devoured all, and his expedition was unimpeded, rushing like water through a gorge, he appeared to those there, filling all the Chaldean nations with uproar and disturbance, having been justly judged for their vain wanderings.
For they were driven, as I have said, such that they even prevailed over Judah without God.
Thus, the vain wandering seized them.
For things born of unbridled passion have come upon them from God, as have their own destructive impieties.
Having suffered this very thing, who then can watch the arch-evil dragon?
For the saying of the Lord has come to pass for him, a word full of wrath.
He himself and the evil powers with him were setting themselves to depart into the abyss.
And they have been consumed just as by fire, and as if being swept down by the power of the Spirit into the lowest depths, like much water.
For they were stirred up in vain through wandering.
For he indeed said, 'I will take the whole inhabited earth in my hand as a spoil, and I will heal it as a thing left behind, and there is no one who escapes me or contends against me' (Isaiah 14:26).

And he realized that God is true according to reality; having transferred the glory that alone is surpassing to the Creator of all into himself, he promised continually that he would be able to hold sway over those on the earth.
They were therefore stirred up in vain wandering, having been judged, and they were seized by it.
For justice, wrath, and punishment were brought upon them because of this very cause.
It is not necessary for you to always rejoice and to enter into my holy places at all times as if celebrating...

title: The Pouring of the Spirit and the Desolation of Carmel
english: For it will be, he says, the promised things, and Israel will be smeared with dung because of its wickedness, until the Spirit from on high comes upon you (Isaiah 32:15).
As we have read in the Acts of the Holy Apostles: they were all together in one place, about the days of the holy Pentecost (Acts 2:1).
And behold, suddenly there came from heaven a sound as of a mighty wind blowing, and it filled the house where they were gathered (Acts 2:2).
And there appeared to them tongues as of fire, distributed, and they sat upon each one of them, and they began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance (Acts 2:3-4).
Therefore when, he says, the Spirit from above and from on high, the Spirit of God, comes upon you who believe, then also the Carmel will be a wilderness (Isaiah 32:15).
The Carmel is either Mount Carmel, a very great mountain in Judea, and wood of date palms, row upon row.
Thus he likens both Jerusalem herself and all the region around dwellings to Carmel, which also has an innumerable multitude of inhabitants.
But it will be, he says, a wilderness and will be counted as a forest (Isaiah 32:15).
By forest he means the wild wood, whose need is for burning, for they cut down the unseasoned woods, and flame…

title: Divine Recognition
english: The psalmist sings through his lyre, saying that he will open his mouth in parables and utter things hidden since the foundation of the world (Matthew 13:35).
He spoke to the Jews in parables.
Therefore, they did not counsel the people, but neither did the deep-voiced one know.
They did not counsel so that the foolish people would not hear.
For if they had counseled, the foolish people would not have heard.
Blessed are those who have recognized the Redeemer.
But there was no understanding for the one hearing.
For the Jews, being foolish, did not discern the voices of their leaders, nor did they distinguish whether they were counseling good or doing the opposite.

Behold, Zion, the city, our Savior, your eyes will see Jerusalem, a wealthy city, tents that will not be shaken, the ropes of its tent will not be broken, for the name of the Lord is great for you (Isaiah 33:20).
A place will be given to you, with broad and spacious rivers and canals.

The face of the lovers of truth, who have recognized the epiphany of Christ, will be brought forth again, saying: whether one speaks of the Church on earth or the one in heaven, the heavenly city, the nourishment of the saints, it is the same, so that even if one calls it the Church on earth or the one in heaven, the meaning is the same.
The divine word takes over the voices of those who, filled with great joy, leap for joy as they have recognized Zion, the place where our salvation, Christ, is found.
They show Zion to others, and the word says that their eyes will see Jerusalem, a rich city, similar to the ancient tabernacle in the wilderness.
The Church has been established and has a firm foundation for being well, for it has unbroken ropes and continuously fixed pegs, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it (Matthew 16:18).
The reason for this is that the name of the Lord is great for those who believe in Christ.
We worship Him as God, as the true Son of the Father, as the Word who became human for the salvation of all.
This, the word says, is the tabernacle that always remains, a place…
translator_notes: The Greek text may be fragmented, and some sentences may be cut off.
The translation of 'ἀσύνετοι' as 'foolish' is chosen over 'ignorant' to convey the sense of lack of understanding.
The word 'Λυτρωτήν' is translated as 'Redeemer' to describe Christ.
The adjective 'εὐρύχωροι' (spacious) is added to the description of the place to maintain accuracy.
The text appears to begin and end mid-sentence, with some clauses possibly missing or fragmented.
